h: Chalk Cliffs, Giant Figures and a Thatched Treasure
p: Drusillas sits at the foot of the South Downs, and the countryside around it is some of the finest in the South East. With a day to spare, you're spoilt for choice.

Alfriston village is just down the lane, with timber-framed pubs, a village green called the Tye and the Alfriston Clergy House, a thatched medieval building that was the very first property bought by the National Trust, back in 1896. Just across the Cuckmere valley, the Long Man of Wilmington is a huge figure cut into the chalk hillside, and nobody is quite sure how old he is, which makes a good puzzle for curious kids.

Follow the Cuckmere River down to the sea and you reach Seven Sisters Country Park, where the river meanders across the flat valley floor to a pebble beach with the white cliffs rising to the east. The walk from the visitor area is fairly flat and buggy-friendly for much of the way. Beachy Head and Eastbourne are a little further along the coast, and Seaford is close for fish and chips on the front.

At Drusillas, the busiest times are school holidays and sunny weekends. Arriving at opening time lets you get round the popular areas before the queues build. Pack a spare set of clothes for little ones; between the play areas and the splash zones, someone usually ends up soggy.
